rules.rule: Extract 'urine' only when part of a structured lab result line with clinical parameters (e.g., RBC, WBC, pH, Nitrite, Protein, Glucose) or culture results. Skip if 'urine' appears in isolated descriptive fields like Color, Appearance, or Sp (specifically in 'Color-Straw Appear-Clear Sp').
Extract 'urine' when it precedes a colon or is followed by a colon and then a clinical test result (e.g., 'URINE RBC-4*', 'URINE CastHy-8*', 'URINE Culture: NO GROWTH').

Do not extract 'urine' if it appears in a non-laboratory context, such as in a section header (e.g., 'URINE CULTURE') or as part of a specimen source (e.g., 'Source: Catheter') without accompanying test values.

Extract 'normal' only when it follows a clinical measurement or assessment and is part of a structured, parenthetical, or comma-separated description of a physiological parameter (e.g., 'LVEF 60-70%', 'free wall motion are normal').
Do not extract 'normal' when it appears in a narrative summary or impression section (e.g., 'IMPRESSION: Normal global and regional biventricular') unless paired with a measurable parameter.

Extract 'normal' when it directly describes a quantified or anatomical finding (e.g., 'left ventricular size is normal', 'aortic valve leaflets are mildly thickened but... normal') in a clinical assessment context.

Extract 'effusion' only when it appears in a clinical imaging or diagnostic section (e.g., ECHO, Admission Labs, DIAGNOSED BY) and is part of a structured description of fluid location (e.g., 'pericardial effusion', 'pleural effusion') with anatomical or morphological detail (e.g., 'circumferential', 'moderate-sized').

Do not extract 'effusion' when it appears in discharge medication or instruction sections, especially when immediately followed by a medication name or dosage (e.g., 'effusion 2. Prednisone...') or when part of a follow-up instruction line.

Do not extract 'effusion' if it appears alone on a line or in a list format without clinical context or anatomical specification (e.g., 'effusion' as a standalone term in a medication list or discharge summary).

Extract 'r' only when it appears as part of a structured, abbreviated anatomical or clinical descriptor (e.g., 'R' in 'R distal dorsal arm' or 'L' in 'L chest') within a lesion or body part listing; skip if standalone or in non-anatomical context.
Do not extract 'r' when it appears in isolation, as a single character in a line, or within a motor/sensory exam line (e.g., 'R 3 3 3 3 1') unless followed by a body part or lesion descriptor.

Extract 'r' only when part of a paired anatomical notation (e.g., 'R' or 'L') preceding a lesion or body site (e.g., 'R distal dorsal arm'), and when the pattern matches clinical documentation conventions for laterality.

Extract 'seizures' when it appears in clinical narrative context indicating a neurological event, especially in HPI, hospital course, or discharge instructions, and is linked to symptoms, evaluation, or treatment.

Do not extract 'seizures' when it appears in a family history or social history section as a negative finding (e.g., 'No seizures') unless followed by clinical context indicating active or past neurological events.

Extract 'seizures' only when it is part of a clinical description involving episodes, events, or diagnostic evaluation; skip if used in passive or non-clinical phrasing (e.g., 'likely triggered by seizures').
Extract 'ct' only when part of a structured imaging order or report context (e.g., 'CT torso', 'CT-torso', 'CT on ___ showed'), indicating a diagnostic imaging study.
Do not extract 'ct' when it appears in narrative or impression sections without anatomical or procedural context (e.g., 'CT with contrast is not able to provide...').
Extract 'ct' only if followed by a body region (e.g., 'torso', 'abdomen', 'chest') or a modifier (e.g., 'with contrast', 'prior to admission'), indicating a specific imaging study.
Extract 'ldl' only when it appears in a structured, clinical checklist or assessment context (e.g., 'LDL documented?', 'LDL >100') within sections like Brief Hospital Course or Discharge Planning.
Do not extract 'ldl' when it appears in narrative text as a standalone value (e.g., 'LDL 149') without accompanying clinical decision or structured assessment language.
Extract 'ldl' only if immediately followed by a clinical threshold, action, or assessment (e.g., 'LDL >100', 'LDL = 62') in a checklist or structured format.

Extract 'cxr' only when it appears in a clinical imaging or diagnostic context, especially when followed by findings, abnormalities, or procedural actions (e.g., 'CXR revealed', 'CXR demonstrated', 'CXR evidence of').

Do not extract 'cxr' when it appears in a procedural or equipment section (e.g., 'CXR (___):') or as part of a line item listing devices (e.g., 'PICC line terminating in SVC') without diagnostic content.

Extract 'cxr' only if it is part of a sentence or phrase describing imaging findings, interpretations, or clinical conclusions (e.g., 'CXR showed', 'CXR revealed'), not when used as a standalone label or header.
